title.narrative: Lifesaving Cholera Outbreak Response to support vulnerable communities (IDPs/Returnees and Host communities) in Central and West Gondar Zones, Amhara Region

description.narrative: ltpgtEthiopia continues to face a widespread cholera outbreak, with over 27,000 confirmed cases and 270 deaths reported across the country. The Amhara Region, particularly Central and West Gondar Zones, has become one of the most affected areas due to recurrent conflict, mass displacement, and poor WASH infrastructure. Within these zones, woredas such as Quara, Alefa, Chilga 1, TachArmachiho, West Dembia, Gendawah Town, Takusa and East Belessa have experienced surges in cholera transmission and fatalities. Internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, and vulnerable host communities are at greatest risk, living in overcrowded shelters with limited access to clean water, sanitation, and healthcare.ltbrgtIn response, Faith in Action (FIA)—a national, women-led organization with extensive experience in WASH and health programming—is Proposed a six-month emergency cholera response titled: “Lifesaving Cholera Outbreak Response to support vulnerable communities (IDPs/Returnees and Host communities) in Central and West Gondar Zones, Amhara Region.” The intervention aims to reduce cholera-related morbidity and mortality by improving access to safe water, sanitation, and health services, while strengthening community-level disease prevention and control.ltbrgtThe project will directly benefit 8081 people, targeting IDPs, returnees, and at-risk host communities in the 8 affected woredas. Key activities include rehabilitating and solarizing water systems, distributing WASH supplies and water treatment chemical constructing emergency latrines and handwashing stations deploying/strengthening rapid response health teams and support Cholera Treatment Centres (CTCs) with Oral Rehydration Points (ORPs) with critical medical supplies. Community Health Volunteers (CHVs) will lead hygiene promotion campaigns through door-to-door education, group sessions, and RCCE (Risk Communication and Community Engagement) efforts, emphasizing handwashing, safe water handling, and early care-seeking behaviours.ltbrgtFIA will collaborate closely with local government health and water bureaus, humanitarian clusters, and existing coordination platforms to avoid duplication, share data, and ensure harmonized response efforts. The project builds on FIA’s current cholera response intervention in Quara Woreda and will also expand activities to Alefa, Chilga 1, TachArmachiho, West Dembia, Gendawah Town, Takusa and East Belessa. This scale-up will leverage existing infrastructure, partnerships, and trained staff, enabling fast and cost-effective delivery.ltbrgtMonitoring, evaluation, and accountability will be embedded throughout the project using sex- and age-disaggregated data, regular field verification, community feedback mechanisms, and participatory assessments. All activities will be inclusive and protection-sensitive, with special attention to the needs of women, children, persons with disabilities, and the elderly. As a local organization, FIA ensures that 100% of implementation is community-led, with no pass-through arrangements.ltbrgtUltimately, this project presents a timely and lifesaving intervention aligned with Ethiopia’s 2025 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) and national cholera response strategy. By combining health and WASH actions and emphasizing localization, FIA will help prevent further loss of life and restore dignity to vulnerable populations in one of Ethiopia’s hardest to reach both zones in Amhara region.ltbrgtlt/pgt
